articleBody:
The Greater Miami Convention & Visitors Bureau is bringing back Miami Spice Restaurant Month for its 25th year, running from August 1 through September 30, 2026. This year marks a notable evolution for the event, which introduces a new Reserve tier alongside the traditional pricing structure, giving diners additional options at higher-end establishments.

Miami Spice has long served as a cornerstone of the region's culinary calendar, leveraging the slower summer season to draw both residents and tourists into restaurants they might not otherwise visit. By offering significant discounts on multi-course meals, the program addresses the dip in dining traffic during the hotter months while allowing restaurants to showcase their menus and service to new audiences. The 25-year history of the program demonstrates its endurance as a marketing tool and its deep integration into Miami's restaurant culture.

The addition of a Reserve tier this year represents a strategic shift in how the program serves its participants. Rather than a one-size-fits-all discount structure, restaurants can now position themselves at different price points and experience levels, allowing fine-dining establishments to participate without devaluing their offerings. This tiered approach reflects an increasingly sophisticated dining market in Miami and gives diners more choice in how they engage with the promotion.

With over 300 restaurants participating, Miami Spice covers a broad spectrum of cuisines, price ranges, and dining styles across the greater Miami area. The program has become a reliable annual event that restaurants plan around, using the two-month window to drive covers, test seasonal menus, and cultivate repeat customers. For visitors and residents alike, it remains one of the most accessible ways to experience the breadth of Miami's food scene at reduced rates.

The continuation and expansion of Miami Spice underscores the GMCVB's commitment to positioning dining as a core pillar of Miami's tourism and lifestyle appeal. As competition among dining destinations intensifies, programs like this one help maintain Miami's reputation as a food-forward city while providing tangible economic benefits to the hospitality industry during periods when tourism naturally dips.

Miami's bar scene is being examined through the lens of refined elegance in a new guide from Miami Curated, which draws parallels to one of New York's most storied cocktail establishments. The publication explores five wonderful Miami bars that share a commitment to timeless sophistication—a quality exemplified by the King Cole Bar at the St. Regis New York, one of the writer's favorite destinations when visiting Manhattan.

The King Cole Bar, located within the St. Regis New York at 2 East 55th Street in Midtown Manhattan, embodies the aesthetic that Miami Curated seeks to highlight. The hotel itself, completed in 1904 to designs by Trowbridge & Livingston and later expanded with an annex by Sloan & Robertson in 1927, was originally developed by John Jacob Astor IV and remains a symbol of luxury hospitality. Today, operated by Marriott International and holding both Forbes five-star and AAA five-diamond ratings, the St. Regis represents a particular vision of elegance that transcends passing trends.

Stepping into the King Cole Bar, as the writer notes, feels like an immersion into a bygone era—a time when elegance was a deeply desired way of life. The bar's design and atmosphere preserve the formality and craftsmanship of mid-twentieth-century luxury, a sensibility that stands in stark contrast to modern fashion's shift toward the casual. This tension between contemporary informality and preserved sophistication forms the heart of Miami Curated's exploration.

The five Miami bars highlighted in the guide appear selected for their commitment to similar values: spaces where guests are invited to engage with a more formal, intentional approach to hospitality. Whether through design, service standards, or drink programs, these establishments maintain an aesthetic discipline that contemporary venues often abandon. According to Miami Curated, such spaces serve an important function in a cultural moment dominated by casualness.

The appeal of these venues extends beyond mere aesthetics.
